802	Come see how it is written there.
803	It is written very similarly, only with a certain difference, which is the difference.
804	Let's first look again at this verse, verse 1 in chapter 8 of Shmuel II.
805	"And it came to pass after this that David smote the Philistines and subdued them, and David took
806	the meteg haama out of the hand of the Philistines."
807	Note the pair of words meteg haama, which, as mentioned, is the bridle of rule, but it is not
808	exactly explained what it is.
809	When we go to Divrei HaYamim I, chapter 18, verse 1, something very similar is written: "And it came
810	to pass after this that David smote the Philistines and subdued them, and took Gat
811	and its towns out of the hand of the Philistines."
812	It does not say here meteg haama, it says Gat

814	Gat was the capital city of the Philistines
815	among those five cities.
816	I already mentioned in the last class that we find Avimelech king of Gerar
817	in the time of Avraham Avinu.
818	That is, the rule over the Philistines in the time of the Patriarchs, which is many, many years before
819	that, was in Gerar.
820	When we reach the time of King David and the period before him, we do not find Gerar
821	appearing at all as a central city among the cities of the Philistines.
822	Which was the central city among the Philistine cities in David's time?
823	Gat.
824	Its king was named Achish, king of Gat,
825	to whom David at one point had to flee because of Shaul, at the time when Shaul was still king.
826	Here it says, "and he took Gat," Gat and its towns, "out of the hand of the Philistines."
827	Gat and its towns means Gat and the rest of the Philistine cities, which are Ashdod, Ashkelon, Ekron,
828	whom did I forget?
829	And Aza of course, yes.
830	Gat was the center of the kingdom, and therefore there the meteg haama is found.
831	Let's see Rashi on the verse in Shmuel, meteg haama. Rashi says,
832	"And in Divrei HaYamim it is written, 'and David took Gat out of the hand of the Philistines.'
833	And it is called meteg haama because it is a rod that rules over all the Philistines."
834	A metropolis of kings, a metropolis of kings.
835	"For we did not find among all the lords of the Philistines, in Aza, Ashdod, Ekron and Ashkelon, a kingship,
836	but only in Gat,
837	as it is written, 'Achish king of Gat.'"
838	Meteg haama is the goad of wood, which is essentially the tribe,
839	that is, the pole, or if you will, the staff, the scepter.
